req.title: Return DELETE request metadata
req.statement: The system shall respond to DELETE /delete with JSON including url, args, headers, form, data, files, json and origin.

doc.reasoning: The requirement mandates that DELETE /delete returns HTTP 200 with a JSON body containing exactly the keys: url, args, headers, form, data, files, json, and origin. Tests are designed to: (1) verify the positive path with a plain DELETE request, (2) verify query-string args are reflected, (3) verify JSON body is reflected, (4) verify form data is reflected, (5) test that a wrong HTTP method (GET) returns 405, (6) test boundary of empty vs non-empty body, and (7) verify all required keys are present with exact values. Each test uses exact-value assertions to maximize mutation kill rate.

tests.name: test_delete_plain_returns_200_with_required_keys
actions: Send DELETE /delete with no body or query params
expected: JSON body contains keys: url, args, headers, form, data, files, json, origin

tests.name: test_delete_with_query_args_reflected
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_delete_with_query_args_reflected():
    r = client.delete('/delete?foo=bar&baz=qux')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.get_json()
    assert body is not None
    assert body['args'] == {'foo': 'bar', 'baz': 'qux'}
    assert 'foo=bar' in body['url'] or 'baz=qux' in body['url']

test_delete_with_query_args_reflected()

tests.name: test_delete_with_json_body_reflected
actions: Send DELETE /delete with Content-Type: application/json and JSON body {"key": "value"}
expected: data key contains the raw JSON string
tests.executable:
import json
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_delete_with_json_body_reflected():
    payload = json.dumps({'key': 'value'})
    r = client.delete(
        '/delete',
        data=payload,
        content_type='application/json'
    )
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.get_json()
    assert body is not None
    assert body['json'] == {'key': 'value'}
    assert body['json']['key'] == 'value'
    assert body['form'] == {}

test_delete_with_json_body_reflected()

tests.name: test_delete_with_form_data_reflected
actions: Send DELETE /delete with form-encoded body field=hello
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_delete_with_form_data_reflected():
    r = client.delete(
        '/delete',
        data={'field': 'hello'},
        content_type='application/x-www-form-urlencoded'
    )
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.get_json()
    assert body is not None
    assert body['form'] == {'field': 'hello'}
    assert body['json'] is None
    assert body['args'] == {}

test_delete_with_form_data_reflected()

tests.name: test_delete_url_field_contains_delete_path
actions: Inspect url field in response body
expected: url field is a string containing '/delete'
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_delete_url_field_contains_delete_path():
    r = client.delete('/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.get_json()
    assert body is not None
    assert isinstance(body['url'], str)
    assert body['url'].endswith('/delete')
    assert 'delete' in body['url']

test_delete_url_field_contains_delete_path()

tests.name: test_delete_headers_reflected_in_response
actions: Send DELETE /delete with custom header X-Test-Header: sentinel
expected: headers dict in response contains X-Test-Header with value sentinel
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_delete_headers_reflected_in_response():
    r = client.delete(
        '/delete',
        headers={'X-Test-Header': 'sentinel'}
    )
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.get_json()
    assert body is not None
    assert isinstance(body['headers'], dict)
    headers_lower = {k.lower(): v for k, v in body['headers'].items()}
    assert headers_lower.get('x-test-header') == 'sentinel'

test_delete_headers_reflected_in_response()

tests.name: test_delete_exact_top_level_keys
actions: Inspect all top-level keys in response JSON
expected: Response JSON has exactly the keys: url, args, headers, form, data, files, json, origin
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_delete_exact_top_level_keys():
    r = client.delete('/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.get_json()
    assert body is not None
    expected_keys = {'url', 'args', 'headers', 'form', 'data', 'files', 'json', 'origin'}
    actual_keys = set(body.keys())
    assert expected_keys == actual_keys

test_delete_exact_top_level_keys()
